---
title: "C FFI API"
---

The C API embeds gridwell in any language with C interop. Before 1.0 it may still
change between releases.
The header is
[`crates/gridwell-ffi/include/gridwell.h`](https://github.com/rich-iannone/gridwell/blob/main/crates/gridwell-ffi/include/gridwell.h).
It is generated from the Rust source by cbindgen, and a test fails if the committed
copy goes stale, so the header is the authoritative reference. The summary below
mirrors it.

## Types

```c
typedef struct GridwellTable GridwellTable;   // opaque
typedef struct GridwellError GridwellError;   // opaque

typedef struct GridwellTextResult {
    char *text;     // NUL-terminated UTF-8; null on failure
    size_t len;     // bytes, excluding the terminator
} GridwellTextResult;

typedef struct GridwellBinaryResult {
    uint8_t *data;  // null on failure
    size_t len;
} GridwellBinaryResult;
```

## Error codes

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_PARSE` | Invalid UTF-8 or JSON, or JSON that isn't a table IR |
| 2 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_VALIDATE` | The IR failed validation; the message lists the errors |
| 3 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_RENDER` | A writer failed, the format name is unknown, or a binary format was passed to `gridwell_render_text` (or a text one to `gridwell_render_binary`) |
| 4 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_INVALID_ARG` | A required pointer was null, or a string wasn't UTF-8 |
| 5 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_PANIC` | An internal panic was caught at the boundary (always a gridwell bug; please report it) |
| 6 | `GRIDWELL_ERR_OPTIONS` | The writer options are invalid: malformed JSON, not an object, an unknown option, a wrong type, or a value out of range |

No Rust panic ever unwinds into C: each function catches panics and reports them as
`GRIDWELL_ERR_PANIC`.

## Functions

```c
// Parse
GridwellTable *gridwell_parse_ir(const char *json, size_t len, GridwellError **err);

// Validate: null on success, else an error listing every problem, one per line.
GridwellError *gridwell_validate(const GridwellTable *table);

// Render text (html, latex, typst, rtf, svg, ansi, pandoc, quarto).
// Both render functions validate first: invalid IR returns an empty result and an
// error with code GRIDWELL_ERR_VALIDATE whose message lists the validation errors.
GridwellTextResult gridwell_render_text(
    const GridwellTable *table, const char *format, GridwellError **err);

// Render binary (docx, xlsx, pptx)
GridwellBinaryResult gridwell_render_binary(
    const GridwellTable *table, const char *format, GridwellError **err);

// The same with writer options: a JSON object, or null for the defaults.
GridwellTextResult gridwell_render_text_with_options(
    const GridwellTable *table, const char *format, const char *options,
    GridwellError **err);
GridwellBinaryResult gridwell_render_binary_with_options(
    const GridwellTable *table, const char *format, const char *options,
    GridwellError **err);

// Warnings, one message per line ("\n"-separated, no trailing newline): first
// "[NEWER_IR_VERSION] …" for a table of a newer minor IR version, then what the
// format can't express, one "[UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE] …" each; an empty string if
// none. A null format means every format. Validates first, as rendering does. Free the result
// with gridwell_free_text_result.
GridwellTextResult gridwell_warnings(
    const GridwellTable *table, const char *format, GridwellError **err);

// Formats: a static comma-separated list of names (do not free), and a name's kind
// (GRIDWELL_FORMAT_TEXT, GRIDWELL_FORMAT_BINARY or GRIDWELL_FORMAT_UNKNOWN).
const char *gridwell_format_names(void);
int32_t gridwell_format_kind(const char *format);

// Error inspection
const char *gridwell_error_message(const GridwellError *err);  // valid until freed
int32_t gridwell_error_code(const GridwellError *err);         // 0 if err is null

// Memory management (all accept null / failed results)
void gridwell_free_table(GridwellTable *table);
void gridwell_free_error(GridwellError *err);
void gridwell_free_text_result(GridwellTextResult result);
void gridwell_free_binary_result(GridwellBinaryResult result);
```

Every `err` out-parameter may be null if you don't need the error. Format names are
case-insensitive. See [Writer Options](../guide/writer-options.qmd) for each format's
options. See [Warnings](../schema/validation.qmd#warnings) for what each format warns
about.

## Example

A program that renders a table IR file to LaTeX:

```{.c filename="example.c"}
#include "gridwell.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* The whole file, or NULL. */
static char *read_file(const char *path, size_t *len) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    char *buf = NULL;
    size_t cap = 0, n = 0, got;
    do {
        if (n == cap) {
            char *bigger = realloc(buf, cap = cap ? 2 * cap : 4096);
            if (!bigger) { free(buf); fclose(f); return NULL; }
            buf = bigger;
        }
        got = fread(buf + n, 1, cap - n, f);
        n += got;
    } while (got > 0);
    fclose(f);
    *len = n;
    return buf;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s TABLE.json\n", argv[0]);
        return 2;
    }
    size_t len;
    char *json = read_file(argv[1], &len);
    if (!json) {
        perror(argv[1]);
        return 1;
    }

    GridwellError *err = NULL;
    GridwellTable *table = gridwell_parse_ir(json, len, &err);
    free(json);
    if (!table) {
        fprintf(stderr, "parse error: %s\n", gridwell_error_message(err));
        gridwell_free_error(err);
        return 1;
    }

    GridwellTextResult result = gridwell_render_text(table, "latex", &err);
    gridwell_free_table(table);  /* the result doesn't borrow from the table */
    if (!result.text) {
        fprintf(stderr, "error %d: %s\n", (int)gridwell_error_code(err),
                gridwell_error_message(err));
        gridwell_free_error(err);
        return 1;
    }
    fwrite(result.text, 1, result.len, stdout);
    gridwell_free_text_result(result);
    return 0;
}
```

Built and run on the [getting-started](../guide/getting-started.qmd#first-table)
table, and on an invalid one:

```{.bash filename="Example output"}
$ ./example hello.json
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
Name & Score \\
\midrule
Alice & 95 \\
Bob & 87 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
$ ./example broken_table.json
error 2: table IR failed validation with 2 errors
  - [COL_COUNT] tbody group 0 row 0 has 4 cells but config.table_cols is 3
  - [SPAN_OVERFLOW_RIGHT] Cell at tbody group 1 (row=0, col=2) has colspan=2 but table only has 3 columns (would need col index up to 3)
```

## Linking

Build the library with `cargo build --release -p gridwell-ffi`. That produces
`libgridwell_ffi.{so,dylib}` and `libgridwell_ffi.a` in `target/release/`. Then:

```bash
cc -o example example.c -I crates/gridwell-ffi/include -L target/release -lgridwell_ffi
```

`crates/gridwell-ffi/tests/c/smoke.c` is a complete working example. The test suite
compiles it as C99, as C++, and under AddressSanitizer.
